summary: This is a React component that displays code snippets with optional explanations and syntax highlighting. It supports two explanation modes: line-by-line tooltips (when eli5json is provided) and a collapsible narrative summary (when eli5summary exists). The component intelligently detects the programming language from props, filenames, or children, applies appropriate styling and icons, and handles copying code to clipboard while properly displaying hidden control characters.

explanations.55: This function recursively searches through React child elements to find a className containing 'language-xyz' pattern, which indicates the programming language. It needs to dig through potentially nested child elements because the language hint might not be on the immediate child.
explanations.329: This checks if a character code represents a control character (like ESC, tab, etc.) that shouldn't be displayed as-is in HTML. It excludes tab (0x09), newline (0x0a), and carriage return (0x0d) because those are safe and useful to show.
explanations.339: This function converts invisible control characters into their Unicode 'control picture' equivalents (like turning ESC into the visible symbol ␛) so they appear in the display but the actual bytes stay unchanged for copying.
explanations.365: This stores a reference to a timeout ID so it can be cleared later if the user copies again before the 1-second 'copied' message expires.
explanations.375: This cleanup function runs when the component unmounts to clear any pending timeout, preventing memory leaks.
explanations.405: This looks up the Prism grammar object for the detected language; if not found, it falls back to plaintext or a basic language to avoid errors.
explanations.409: useTokenize breaks the code into syntax-highlighted tokens while preserving multi-line tokens intact (unlike naive split-by-newline approaches that would break tokens across line boundaries).
explanations.414: This removes any synthetic empty 'newline' token that useTokenize adds when code ends with a newline, so line numbers stay aligned with the eli5 annotations object.
explanations.423: This computes where the tooltip should appear relative to its badge button — above it and right-aligned — using the button's position on screen.
explanations.442: This attaches scroll and resize listeners while a tooltip is open so the tooltip stays glued to its badge as the page scrolls or the viewport changes.
explanations.457: The className combines the language class (for syntax highlighting) with the component's own styles.
explanations.476: The map renders each line of code tokens as a separate row, converting the token index to a 1-based line number for matching against the eli5 annotations.
explanations.495: This callback stores a reference to each badge button by its line number so positionTooltip() can later measure where to place the tooltip.
explanations.533: createPortal renders the tooltip into document.body instead of the normal DOM tree, which lets it appear above any overflow:hidden ancestors that would otherwise clip it.
explanations.561: useId generates a unique ID for the summary disclosure element so the toggle button can reference it via aria-controls for accessibility.
explanations.565: This sets the max-height to either the actual scrollHeight (to show all content) or 0 (to hide it), with CSS transitions making it animate smoothly between states.
explanations.632: This safely parses the eli5json string (injected by a build plugin) into a JavaScript object, returning null if it's missing or malformed instead of crashing.
explanations.644: This checks that eli5summary is a non-empty string; trimmed and stored or set to null if absent, so the summary block only renders when there's actual content.
explanations.656: This priority chain determines the language: first check the pluginLang prop, then search children for a language-xyz className, then extract from filename extension, finally default to plaintext.
explanations.679: substitutePlainText swaps in user-provided variable values (like {{name}}) directly into the plain-text code before it goes to Prism for syntax highlighting.
explanations.685: substituteChildren does the same variable substitution but within React elements, wrapping the substituted values with VarToken to give them special styling that shows they're user-provided.
explanations.698: This checks whether the component should use the line-by-line Eli5CodeBlock renderer (when annotations exist or there are control characters) versus the simpler Docusaurus CodeBlock.
explanations.708: This extracts just the filename portion from a full path (removing any directory prefix) and lowercases it for consistent comparison.
explanations.716: This recognizes various Docker-related filenames (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yaml, etc.) to apply Docker-specific styling and icons even if the language detection would normally pick something else.
explanations.732: This picks the final styling variant: explicit variant prop takes priority, then special cases for Docker/Docusaurus files, then the default mapping for the detected language, finally falling back to 'none'.
explanations.740: This looks up a CSS class name from the styles object using the variant key (e.g., variant_docker) to apply language-specific visual styling.
explanations.745: These destructure the icon metadata (icon name, CSS class, accessibility label) from the variantIcons lookup, using the 'none' variant as fallback if the detected variant has no icon defined.
explanations.747: This determines what text to show at the top of the snippet block, preferring explicit title, then filename, then language name in uppercase, finally a generic 'Snippet' label if nothing else is available.
